title: perf(cli): keep read-only commands on cold paths

nodes.body:
Codex review: needs maintainer review before merge. _Reviewed August 2, 2026, 5:37 AM ET / 09:37 UTC._ # ClawSweeper review ## What this changes The branch keeps nine read-only CLI commands cold by skipping unnecessary plugin validation and loading, reusing a single plugin metadata snapshot for channel listings, and returning the first `usage.cost` Gateway response instead of polling for cache freshness. ## Merge readiness ⚠️ **Ready for maintainer review - 5 items remain** This PR remains necessary: it extends the recently merged CLI cold-path work to additional read-only commands and removes command-local metadata rediscovery. The manifest-first snapshot design matches the repository’s hot-path guidance, and no concrete patch defect was established, but the `maintainer` label requires human handling and the local sibling Codex source required to independently verify the `models status` Codex-runtime contract is unavailable. **Priority:** P2 **Reviewed head:** `5b701d953dd8861ea75740f869e8364285e1a7ee` **Owner decision:** Required. See [Decision needed](#decision-needed). ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | The branch has strong focused behavior evidence and coherent manifest-first ownership, with a remaining compatibility decision and unavailable local Codex-contract check. | | **Proof confidence** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | Sufficient (live_output): The PR body supplies after-fix production and local command timings plus route-level cold-import and one-RPC assertions; a maintainer still needs to confirm the supported all-agent timeout envelope before merge. | | **Patch quality** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | No actionable review findings were identified. | ## Verification | Check | Result | Evidence | |---|---|---| | **Real behavior** | Verified | Sufficient (live_output): The PR body supplies after-fix production and local command timings plus route-level cold-import and one-RPC assertions; a maintainer still needs to confirm the supported all-agent timeout envelope before merge. | | **Evidence reviewed** | 6 items | Manifest-first channel-list path: The branch reads valid core configuration while skipping plugin-schema validation, resolves one process-stable metadata snapshot, and passes its discovery/index facts to the channel readers instead of rediscovering plugins per catalog row.
Gateway owns cached usage summaries: The Gateway has a dedicated `usage.cost` handler and cache-loading path, supporting the branch’s removal of CLI-side freshness polling while preserving the returned cache-status information.
Usage-cost command contract changed deliberately: Current main gives `gateway usage-cost` a five-minute command default and polls for a fresh cache; the branch instead sends one RPC through the ordinary transport options, retaining explicit `--timeout` handling but changing the default wait behavior to the standard RPC timeout. | | **Findings** | None | None. | | **Security** | None | None. | ## How this fits together The CLI’s startup policy decides whether a command performs local config and plugin work before dispatching to a local projection or the running Gateway. This PR keeps read-only commands on manifest-backed control-plane data and lets the Gateway own cached usage-summary refreshes. ```mermaid flowchart LR CLI[Read-only CLI command] --> Policy[Startup policy] Policy --> Config[Core config projection] Config --> Metadata[Plugin metadata snapshot] Metadata --> Local[Local list or status projection] Gateway[Gateway RPC] --> Usage[Usage summary] Local --> Output[JSON or text output] Usage --> Output ``` ## Decision needed | Question | Recommendation | |---|---| | Should `gateway usage-cost` adopt the standard 10-second default RPC timeout now that it returns cached or in-flight summaries immediately, rather than preserve its former five-minute freshness-wait budget? | **Accept immediate cached summaries:** Keep the one-RPC implementation and standard timeout, with the Gateway continuing background refresh ownership. | Why: This is an operator-visible compatibility choice: the branch intentionally changes latency and freshness semantics, and supported high-volume all-agent deployments determine whether the shorter default is safe. ## Before merge - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P2)** - `gateway usage-cost` changes its default transport timeout from five minutes to the standard 10-second RPC timeout while intentionally stopping cache-freshness polling; confirm that cached all-agent summaries remain safely responsive under supported production load. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - The `models status` change touches Codex runtime availability, but this review could not inspect the required sibling Codex source because `../codex` is absent. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - The protected `maintainer` label requires explicit human handling before merge. - [ ] **Complete next step (P2)** - No mechanical repair is identified; human confirmation is needed for the usage-cost timeout compatibility choice and the required Codex dependency-contract check.

### Review metrics | Metric | Value | Why it matters | |---|---|---| | **Startup-policy changes** | 9 read-only command paths | The branch broadens cold-path startup behavior across several operator commands, making preserved validation and timeout contracts material before merge. | ### Stored data model Persistent data-model change detected: `persistent cache schema: src/cli/gateway-cli.coverage.test.ts`, `serialized state: src/cli/models-status-route-cold-imports.test.ts`, `vector/embedding metadata: src/channels/plugins/read-only.ts`, `vector/embedding metadata: src/cli/channels-list-route-cold-imports.test.ts`, `vector/embedding metadata: src/commands/channels.list.test.ts`, `vector/embedding metadata: src/commands/channels/list.ts`. Confirm migration or upgrade compatibility proof before merge. ### Merge-risk options **Maintainer options:** 1. **Confirm one-RPC timeout behavior (recommended)** Verify a representative all-agent cached and refreshing usage summary under the intended production topology before accepting the shorter default timeout. 2. **Keep the prior timeout default** Preserve the five-minute command default while removing only the freshness polling if operators need more than the standard RPC window. 3. **Defer the semantic change** Pause or split the usage-cost portion if the supported latency envelope cannot be demonstrated before merge. ### Technical review Best possible solution: Merge only after a maintainer confirms the one-RPC usage-cost timeout behavior is acceptable for supported all-agent deployments and a reviewer with the sibling Codex checkout verifies the lazy runtime-availability contract; otherwise retain the manifest-first cold-path changes and narrow only the affected command behavior. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Yes for the code-path change: current main polls `usage.cost` until freshness with a five-minute default, while the branch performs one RPC; the reported large-plugin timing topology was not independently available in this read-only checkout. Is this the best way to solve the issue? Mostly yes: the prepared metadata snapshot follows the repository’s manifest-first, process-stable metadata model, but the shorter usage-cost default timeout and Codex runtime contract need explicit confirmation before this is the best complete solution. - The Codex contract was rechecked directly in sibling source. `account/read` is declared as typed `GetAccountParams` / `GetAccountResponse` in `../codex/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/common.rs:1192`; dispatch is `../codex/codex-rs/app-server/src/message_processor.rs:1372`; the account processor owns refresh/config/provider account-state resolution in `../codex/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/account_processor.rs:1010`; and the response contract is `../codex/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/account.rs:484`. The lazy OpenClaw payload check does not change this protocol or ownership.
